ground_truth: Track income/expenses to find savings gaps.  Apply 50/30/20 budgeting with priority on needs.  Build a starter emergency fund ($500 → $1000 → 1 month expenses).  Prioritize paying down high-interest debt.  Consolidate debts if necessary.  Build credit early.  Begin tax optimization basics.  Use low-cost insurance to manage risk.

Focus on capital preservation.  Keep majority in cash/cash-equivalents.  Avoid high-volatility assets.  Use conservative allocation: high bonds, very low stocks.  Allocation goal is stability until emergency fund + debts are under control.

Maintain a consistent 50/30/20 budget.  Build full emergency fund (3–6 months).  Continue structured debt payoff.  Increase retirement contributions (401k, IRA).  Review tax strategy annually.  Use insurance to reduce risk.  Begin medium-term goal planning (home, education).

Moderate allocation: mix of stocks, bonds, cash.  Diversify within each asset class (domestic/international).  Rebalance periodically.  Match allocation to goals and time horizon.  Use target-date funds or basic rule-of-100 for guidance.

Maximize long-term retirement contributions (toward IRS limits).  Use tax-optimized vehicles (401k, 403b, IRA).  Maintain 6–12 months emergency fund.  Optimize taxes proactively (W-4 adjustments, deductions).  Begin estate planning (trusts, wills, POA).  Long-term financial goal setting (college, early retirement).

Aggressive allocation heavy on equities.  Higher proportion of growth assets.  Diversify across global stocks.  Accept higher volatility for long-term returns.  Gradually rebalance to preserve gains as goals get closer.  Maintain strategic allocation based on age + goals + risk tolerance.
